cases.observed: The new-watchtower prompt produced an unfinished response repeating unrelated historical cliff operations and IDs; no Blender model was generated.
cases.verified_correction: Do not paste historic action payloads or old coordinates. Supply only short transferable lessons and use short stage-specific response schema.
cases.safe_lesson: Do not repeat old rejected actions or object IDs when starting a different asset. Use an original, concise plan for the current object.

cases.observed: Qwen returned syntactically complete creative JSON but supplied a shape primitive parameter object to the explicit-vertex mesh operation and selected architecture scales around 100 meters, creating nonexistent targets on retry.
cases.verified_correction: New assets begin with schema-constrained primitive objects and dimensions 0.15–8 in a small batch; later source-verified cycles can use full Blender mesh, UV, material, sculpt and nodes operations.
cases.safe_lesson: New assets need genuine, proportionate mesh objects before secondary details. Do not use nonexistent objects or substitute primitive arguments for indexed vertices.

cases.observed: Four genuine Qwen-directed Blender primitives exported as an editable BLEND/GLB; image revealed disconnected roof, overlapping masonry and several objects buried at wrong heights. The Qwen critique returned invalid JSON.
cases.verified_correction: Separate geometric sanity from visual certification; return invalid silhouettes to Qwen, require roof tiers, plausible contact and material/structural refinement on a verified existing source.
cases.safe_lesson: When creating an architecture asset, roof and shaft must occupy aligned, different real heights, parts must not be identical overlapping masses, and materials must be deliberately authored. Real Blender success is not art approval.

cases.observed: Real fixed-camera A/B of inherited timber watchtower shows roof and stair distortions from global landmark deformation, not a professional quality improvement.
cases.safe_lesson: For a small timber lookout mesh, do not deform the whole stair and roof assembly with broad landmark brushes. Choose local detail that preserves the existing architectural silhouette and connections.

cases.safe_lesson: For genuine inherited mesh edits, read actual source-relative brush limits and choose stroke distance and radius strictly inside both bounds. Never invent a smaller radius or repeat invalid brush decisions.

cases.observed: On actual Blender fixed-camera timber watchtower images, Qwen 8B named a cylinder RoofOverhang but placed it centrally at WORLD Z 3.27m (roof apex), so it produced a cropped roof-top disc, NOT an attached architectural eave. Positive executable outcome is not aesthetic improvement.
cases.safe_lesson: When adding a timber roof eave or overhang, ensure the ORIGINAL chosen geometry touches an actual X/Y outer roof edge and is below the highest WORLD Z apex; a central roof-top cylinder is not a realistic roof-edge detail. Check matched-camera A/B for visible and coherent improvement.

cases.observed: Authentic Qwen8B professional eave trial from Windows 2026-10-14 failed all 5 plans before Blender. Attempt 1 authored duplicate 3D mesh vertices; attempts 2-4 repeated geometrically disconnected CENTRAL roof apex eaves despite exact explicit measured rejection; attempt 5 chose a volume too thin/tiny to be legible. Zero valid A/B models from this run.
cases.safe_lesson: When full-dimensional tower detail attempts repeatedly fail physical roof attachment or closed-mesh checks, stop repeating the same cylinder-at-apex geometry. Choose another appropriate architectural tool from the Blender source-grounded inventory (selected bevel/extrusion, existing surface adjustment, real edge-attached new part); retain original source and never claim success without real A/B.

cases.observed: Actual Qwen8B chose a selected-face extrude and then a whole-dense-source material replacement plus uv.smart_project. Blender executed the changes, but fixed-camera protected entry pixels differed by 87.6% and staircase by 46.3%, violating original source preservation. Subsequent cycles repeated similarly unsafe plans. No art was approved.
cases.safe_lesson: Do not apply whole-object MATERIAL replacement or UV unwrap to the dense inherited watchtower texture atlas after a small extrude; they damage unrelated door, stair and roof appearance. Choose ONE local structural edit first, reinspect, and perform later material/UV finishing only on a separately created component.

cases.observed: Qwen3-VL 8B edited the genuine old tower three times, always extruding inherited FACE 2326 by WORLD +Z 0.15m with no materials or UV replacement. The camera-matched Blender pixel difference was exactly 0 of 691,200 on each cycle. Source material preservation succeeded, but no visible artistic improvement occurred.
cases.safe_lesson: After an authentic Blender A/B shows ZERO changed pixels for a face extrusion, never repeat the exact face and offset or default to the same Blender operation three times. Change the artistic tactic to a different source-grounded face/edge or compatible tool, and demand a visible result with original timber/door/stair textures intact.

cases.observed: Independent inspection of the original 960x720 Blender camera matched A/B from 2026-10-14: Qwen8B face 325/324 extrudes yielded 0.3601%, 0.19329%, 0.27619%, 0.3601% of pixels above threshold in four cycles, all below 0.6% minimum. No visibly convincing eave architecture or improved composition, although 24 real camera visible faces were measured. No accepted artwork or unity test.
cases.safe_lesson: Four real source camera A/B rejections demonstrate that merely selecting faces ray-visible from the camera is insufficient. After two visually negligible extrudes on the timber Valoria tower, abandon the face-extrusion hypothesis. Change real Blender tool AND artistic approach to a clearly legible attached structural detail with preserved stairs/roof/atlas. Do not count moved vertices or pixel fraction as visual approval.

cases.observed: Qwen4B claimed there were no defects, but genuine same-camera PNGs display a detached 0.6 m cube floating 0.875 m beyond source WORLD Y bounds. It is a new spatial-composition defect. Pixel-change fraction 0.0338064 is visibility only, not aesthetic improvement.
cases.safe_lesson: Real source WORLD Y is [-1.325,1.325] metres. Adding an original primitive centered at Y=2.5 with half-size 0.3 leaves a 0.875m contact gap; don't claim roof attachment because a piece changes pixels or passes a loose scene AABB. Choose a fully new authored design with physically overlapping source world volume and real supporting geometry; preserve original tower and camera, no assistant auto placement.

cases.observed: Left and right original Qwen roof braces occupy exactly the same XYZ coordinates and dimensions. Genuine fixed-camera render depicts a single wood-colored vertical pole protruding behind roof, not distinct timber structural support. No believable roof-edge contact or visual quality gain.
cases.safe_lesson: Qwen may write different descriptive LEFT/RIGHT object names yet assign exactly identical WORLD location, rotation and scale. These are not two structural braces but one doubled overlapping post. For genuine multi-part timber architecture, design physically connected AND spatially distinct members; no component may overlap another by >92% of its volume. Independent A/B must confirm coherent construction rather than count different IDs or changed pixels.
